Because ES module imports evaluate before any of the importING file's own top-level statements (regardless of vi.mock's own separate hoisting), this forced the route module's dependency graph (including the mocked "../lib/buildableEnvelope/roads" module) to load before this test file's own `const BASTROP_LAT = 30.11` (line 42) had run, throwing `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'BASTROP_LAT' before initialization` inside the roads mock factory, which references BASTROP_LAT. I confirmed by stashing the whole diff and re-running against pristine origin/main with the same dummy DATABASE_URL: the pristine file loads fine and reaches the real, expected failure (ECONNREFUSED against the dummy DB, 19 tests skipped) -- proving the hoisting crash was a genuine regression introduced by the new diff, not a pre-existing condition. FIXED by me directly (not re-dispatched, since it was a small, precisely-diagnosed, mechanical correction): moved the constant to a dynamic `const { POINT_RESOLUTION_TIMEOUT_MS } = await import(...)` placed alongside this file's OWN existing established pattern for exactly this situation (the file already does the identical dynamic-import-after-mocks dance for setupRouteTests/resetBrokerageApiKeysForTests/__resetServiceApiKeyCacheForTests at line ~304-310). Re-ran with the dummy DATABASE_URL afterward: file now loads cleanly and collects 22 tests (19 pre-existing + 3 new), all skipped for the same pre-existing real-DB-required reason as the pristine baseline -- confirms the fix, not a new failure mode.
